mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 0.2% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to reduced cost of capital.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.2%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment exceeding 8.0% signals persistent labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous GDP growth above 0.5% and housing starts above 0.5% indicate robust consumer demand and construction activity, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of GDPC1 and HOUST growth fails to predict positive returns when both exceed thresholds (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: High inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually) trigger central bank policy tightening that reduces equity multiples, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of high inflation regime periods (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually).

mechanism_narrative: Industrial production growth above 1.0% monthly indicates expanding manufacturing output that correlates with rising corporate profits, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO growth above 1.0% monthly fails to produce positive 5-day returns in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts below 700.0 units signal weak construction activity and consumer confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days due to reduced economic momentum.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when HOUST < 700.0.

mechanism_narrative: Strong employment growth (PAYEMS > 0.5% monthly) combined with high retail sales (RSAFS > 1.0% monthly) indicates robust consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: The joint signal of PAYEMS and RSAFS growth fails to predict positive returns when both conditions are met (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In post-crisis recovery regimes, unemployment above 7.5% correlates with delayed economic recovery and negative short-term equity returns due to fiscal policy uncertainty.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances during the post-crisis recovery period when UNRATE > 7.5%.
